title: Hotslot throughput coda: adaptive priming and slot granularity
content:
Objective:
- Quick scratch: characterize how micro-slotting ("hotslots") + tiny prefill priming affects throughput and p99 under mixed small+large requests for a 7B decoder-only model (quantized 4-bit path).

Context / why: 
- We see recurring p99 spikes when a stream of small requests interleaves with a few long-context hits. Hypothesis: reserving short-lived hotslots (warm KV + pre-warmed CUDA contexts) for small requests reduces serialization and cold-cache thrash.
- Want cheap tweak to scheduling without cluster resizing.

Experiment matrix (config notes):
- Model: redwood/7b-v1-ql4 (cpu-quantized path off, GPU run).
- HW: a2-1xA100 equiv test node, 40 GB GPU mem.
- Runtime flags: kv-cache enabled (true), continuous-batching (true), slot-size param (slot_ms), priming-tokens=8, prefill-mode=hot (special path).
- Arrival pattern: blended burst: 1000 small requests (avg tokens_out 24) at Poisson lambda 350 r/s for 60s; interleave 10 large requests (avg output tokens 512) randomly at 1–5s intervals.
- Metrics captured: qps, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (server-side), observed batching size, KV cache hit-rate, GPU utilization, context-switch count (hotslot evictions).

Quick run summary (selected runs):
CSV: (slot_ms, priming_tokens, observed_qps, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, kv_hit_pct, slot_evictions)
"slot_ms,priming_tokens,observed_qps,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,kv_hit_pct,slot_evictions"
"10,8,335,18,42,112,87,210"
"25,8,341,19,39,98,91,125"
"50,8,348,20,37,88,93,62"
"100,8,350,21,38,94,94,40"
"25,0,312,22,58,210,46,340"
"25,16,343,18,36,89,95,118"

Observations / notes to self:
- Baseline-ish behaviour: priming_tokens=0 -> massive p99 collapse (210ms) and KV hit-rate ~46%: indicates small requests frequently miss cache after eviction.
- Small slot_ms (10ms) reduces latency but causes lots of slot_evictions -> scheduling overhead visible. 25–50ms seems sweet spot in this HW for our arrival mix.
- Increasing priming_tokens from 0 -> 8 substantially improves kv_hit_pct and p99 (46%->91%). Diminishing returns beyond 8–16 for this profile.
- 50ms slot had best trade-off: qps+latency vs evictions. 100ms increased evictions drop but slightly raised p50/p95 (queueing for the hotslot?). Might be because long requests occasionally steal slots longer than expected. Need trace.
- GPU util stayed ~78–92% across good runs; small slot sizes increased context thrash (observed CUDA stream churn).

Micro-instrumentation notes (what traces showed):
- When a long request arrives during a hotslot window, we observed delayed prefill eviction: hotslot retained but large request triggered an internal preemption path which serialized a ~30ms stall for the micro-batch queue.
- KV cache header shows small requests benefitted from prefix re-use in >90% of success runs; misses coincide with slot_evictions and GC window.

Quick conclusions / practical takeaways:
- For mixed workloads dominated by small requests with occasional long tails:
  - Enable small priming (8 tokens) by default on dedicated pools serving chat/short-completions.
  - Use slot_ms = 25–50ms as default hotslot duration on A100-class nodes; tune down on higher core-count setups.
  - Watch for preemption path latency when large requests arrive — consider a fast-fail fallback that routes long requests to a separate pool (or uses low-priority lanes).
- Cost: priming 8 tokens per small request adds ~2–4 token executions but reduces p99-related error budgets and retries (net win).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Does this generalize to other model families (encoder-decoder, non-ql4 quant)? schedule a sweep across 13B/16B variants.
- Can we make slot allocation adaptive based on measured short-request density rather than fixed ms? sketches below.
- Are there safety concerns (priming content leakage between tenants?) — ensure priming context is synthetic/blank and not prefilled with tenant data.

Sketch: adaptive-slot policy (notes)
- Maintain short-window request counter per worker (sliding 1s).
- If small-request ratio > 70% -> set slot_ms=40 and priming_tokens=8. Else slot_ms=100 and priming_tokens=0.
- Add hysteresis: require 3s stable state to flip to avoid oscillation.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Add a tracepoint that marks 'hotslot-claimed' and 'hotslot-evicted' with reason codes (sched, preempt, mempressure). (ENG-4127)
- [ ] Run 13B ql4 sweep (slot_ms=25/50, priming 8/16) on smaller cluster (ask infra for short window). (owner: Kaiya)
- [ ] Prototype adaptive-slot policy in scheduling branch (PR linked above). (owner: Riley)
- [ ] Validate tenant isolation for priming buffer (security review). (owner: Dara)

Notes to future self: 
- Keep raw traces for the 2025-10-30 11:12AM run (label: hotslot-50ms-8pt). There's a weird ~220ms outlier at t=18s — looks like GC coincident with an infra burst.
- Slack thread (linked) has initial comments from @sanja — check his concern about evictions adding jitter across multi-tenant nodes.

Rough rating (should we ship?):
- Feature-level: low-risk experiment -> default enable for dedicated small-request pools after followups.
- Ops-level: need tracing and eviction telemetry first.

-- end scratch --
summary: Scratchpad: micro-slot "hotslot" experiments for mixed small/large request patterns. Found priming=8 tokens + slot_ms 25-50ms gives best p99 reduction and high KV hit rates; plan adaptive-slot policy and follow-up sweeps.
